title: Fast and efficient genetic transformation of sugar beet by _Agrobacterium rhizogenes_
protocol: Place around 100 seeds into a sterile 250 ml Erlenmeyer flask.
Add 50 ml of hypochlorite/H2O supplemented with Tween-20 while gently mixing and leave for 5 min.
Discard hypochlorite/H2O and wash the seeds 4 times with excess (100 ml) of sterile water.
Dry seeds on a sterilized paper towel for 5 min.
Place the sterilized sugar beet seeds, 2 cm apart (around 10 seeds per plate), with forceps into plates containing solid germination medium.
Seal the plates with parafilm and incubate for 7 days in growth chamber adjusted at 21-23 ºC.
Streak bacteria from glycerol stock onto the surface of LB plates containing the appropriate antibiotics and incubate at 28 ºC for 2 days.
Pick a single colony and suspend in 1 ml liquid LB medium supplemented with antibiotics and incubate with gentle agitation at 28 ºC overnight.
Spread 200 μl of the suspension onto two fresh plates containing the appropriate antibiotics and incubate at 28 ºC overnight.
After 7 days, select healthy, well-developed seedlings for root transformation.
Cut the selected seedlings at the hypocotyl using a sterile blade.
Remove the existing root system from the seedling.
Holding the seedling with forceps, dip the wounded surface of the hypocotyl into the bacterial layer.
Place 5-7 inoculated seedlings on square petri dishes containing co-cultivation medium, half-covered with sterile filter paper.
Cover the wounded surface of each plant with a sterile filter paper.
Seal the petri dishes with parafilm and place them vertically in the growth chamber for 3 days under a 16/8 h photoperiod at 21-23 °C.
Transfer the seedlings to square petri dishes containing emergence medium supplemented with cefotaxime (250 μg m\(^{-1}\)) and appropriate antibiotics, half-covered with filter paper.
Cover the lower part of the seedlings with sterile filter paper.
Seal the dishes with parafilm and place them vertically in the growth chamber.
Monitor regularly for the emergence of hairy roots.
After 10 days, transfer the seedlings onto fresh emergence medium, half-covered with filter paper.
At this time point, ensure that the hairy roots are approximately 4-6 cm in length.
Seedlings with well-developed hairy root systems can be directly used for functional genomics studies.
Maintain seedlings in liquid MS medium under antibiotic selection.
Transfer seedlings to pots and acclimatize plants by gradually decreasing humidity.
Establish an in vitro hairy root culture through clonal propagation.
